**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Longitudinal split of a corn stalk (near ear attachment), showing internal pith tissue
- Pith tissue is orange-brown/tan colored
- Numerous small, uniformly distributed black dots scattered throughout the pith
- Kernels visible at top are brown/discolored
- The black dots appear evenly distributed (not in rows), suggesting microsclerotia rather than pycnidia

**Key distinguishing feature:** The uniform scattering of tiny black dots (microsclerotia) throughout orange-brown pith tissue is the hallmark of Charcoal stalk rot (*Macrophomina phaseolina*).

**Reference comparison:** The Charcoal stalk rot reference showed more advanced shredded/fibrous stage — the test image appears to be an earlier stage where the microsclerotia are visible but tissue hasn't fully shredded yet. The dot density and distribution pattern matches charcoal rot over Diplodia (which shows white mycelium + fewer, larger pycnidia).

The even distribution of microsclerotia throughout the pith distinguishes this from Diplodia (which has white mycelium and larger pycnidia in rows) or Anthracnose (black lesion patterns)."}
